known as daily reference values [DRVs] [Table 11-5]). However, 
food labels use only the term daily value. RDIs provide a large 
margin of safety; in general, the RDI for a nutrient is greater than 
the RDA for a specific age group. As new DRIs are developed in 
various categories, labeling laws are updated. Box 11-3 provides 
tips for reading and understanding food labels.
Nutrient Content Claims
Nutrient content terms such as reduced sodium, fat free, low-
calorie, and healthy must meet government definitions that 
apply to all foods (Box 11-4). For example, lean refers to a serv-
